indicator_name:
• Healthy life expectancy at birth
  • Low-birthweight babies (percentage of births)
area_description:
From the report ‘Counting What Counts – A Compass of Progress for People and Planet’ by the United Nations High-Level Panel on ‘Beyond GDP’:
Good health underpins quality of life and longevity, while poor health directly limits people’s ability to work, learn, and participate in society. Health outcomes are closely linked to material conditions and feed back into income, productivity and social inclusion. Early-life health disadvantages have long-lasting consequences, and population health is a central component of human capital, sustainable development, and quality of life.
